text:
jamie (oncall): incident-bot auto-page: multiple SRV lookup failures in us-west-3 for internal control-plane SRV records. Seeing spikes in job controller errors and several failed healthchecks. Investigating now.

incident-bot: paging oncall jamie (oncall) — alerts: coredns.servfail.rate > 5% in us-west-3 for last 3m, traceroute anomalies detected to control-plane VIPs.

sre-alex: thanks. first quick check: are these pure DNS (CoreDNS) SERVFAILs or upstream egress problems? maria, can you pull route table and VPC route-propagation status for us-west-3?

maria-eng-net: grabbing route table + peering status. seeing delayed route propagation on a subset of AZs (us-west-3a/3c) after a control plane fabric flapping event ~30m ago. Some routes to node ENIs are still tagging as "pending" in the cloud console.

ops-ross: from app logs we're getting both: SRV lookups returning SERVFAIL and direct TCP handshakes timing out in those AZs. Example from pod logs: 

```
E0321 14:52:12.123 kube-proxy: lookup _grpc._tcp.controlplane.svc.cluster.local: server failure
E0321 14:52:12.130 controller: failed to reconcile, retrying
```

jamie (oncall): can we confirm CoreDNS pods in those AZs? maybe a kube-proxy CNI misconfig too. Alex, any quick way to force clients off the affected AZs until we stabilize?

sre-alex: yes. Two parallel mitigations: 1) traffic-manager policy -> prefer-us-west-2 for control-plane routes for 10m (fail open) 2) roll coredns as a daemonset restart in affected AZ nodes to clear caches. I'll coordinate.

maria-eng-net: to be explicit — cloud control plane shows a BGP session flap then partial route withdraw. Some propagated routes are stuck with stale propagation ids. I've opened a support case with the cloud provider, but we should mitigate at our edge.

ops-ross: note: some customers on us-west-3 are seeing 502/504 during deployments. Product customer reporting a single-tenant job failure -> escalated.

bianca-product: marking major-customer A as potentially impacted — they're running scheduled deployments in us-west-3. CC: account team.

incident-bot: action: created incident INC-2026-183945 (sev P1). Notifying execs and posting status page draft.

sre-alex: mitigation plan executed: 
- applied traffic-policy override to prefer us-west-2 for control-plane service routing (propagates via our traffic-manager in ~30s)
- restarted coredns daemonset pods on nodes in us-west-3a/3c with `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/coredns --field-selector spec.nodeName=...` (restarted in stages to avoid full disruption)

jamie (oncall): commands I ran (for record):
```
# verify SRV from inside pod in us-west-3a
kubectl exec -n test nslookup -type=SRV _grpc._tcp.controlplane.svc.cluster.local -- /bin/sh -c "dig +short SRV _grpc._tcp.controlplane.svc.cluster.local" 
# check CoreDNS logs
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/coredns -l k8s-app=coredns --tail=200 | grep SERVFAIL
```

ops-ross: after coredns restart, SRV lookups in restarted nodes returned answers again. Downstream controllers retried successfully. However some node-level TCP paths still hit RTT spikes when the traffic-manager reroute hit a few edge routers.

maria-eng-net: cloud provider acknowledged a regional route-propagation backlog and initiated a targeted reconciliation. They expect resolution in ~20-40m. They recommended not to re-announce routes from our side while they reconcile.

jamie (oncall): customer-impact-bot, do we have numbers on % of requests failing?

customer-impact-bot: detected 8.1% increase in 5xx for control-plane API in us-west-3 over the last 15m. ~12 customers had >5% error rate for at least one minute. No external customer data exfiltration. Severity: degraded availability.

bianca-product: message to impacted customers drafted — holding for confirmation of baseline return before send.

sre-alex: propose post-mitigation steps: 
- add active SRV synthetic checks from each AZ every 30s (alert on >1% SERVFAILs)
- add route-propagation watch to our infra collector (cloudprovider events -> pager on stuck propagation)
- update runbook: when propagation is stuck, prefer traffic-manager override and do staged coredns restarts.

ops-ross: also suggest lowering TTL on SRV records for control-plane during maintenance windows so cached entries don't bake bad state.

jamie (oncall): handing off to alex for next watch cycle. I'm going offline in 25m but will re-check on second page. Summary: P1, root cause appears to be regional route-propagation backlog after fabric flap causing CoreDNS to return SERVFAIL for SRV queries for endpoints in affected AZs. Mitigations applied: traffic-manager reroute to us-west-2, staged coredns restarts, cloud provider reconciliation in progress.

sre-alex: thanks. taking over watch. Currently monitoring: SRV SERVFAIL rate, control-plane 5xx, route-propagation state. If any customer signals escalate to oncall paging.

incident-bot: update: traffic-policy override active. Monitoring thresholds remain elevated.

(m ~ 35m later)

sre-alex: update — cloud provider reports reconciliation complete for the remaining stuck propagations ~+34m. Verified route entries show "active" across AZs. Rolling back traffic-policy to normal routing in 5m to verify stability.

ops-ross: after rollback, no surge in 5xx; metrics trending back to baseline. SRV SERVFAILs down to 0.2%.

jamie (oncall): good. final checks: runbooks updated, postmortem owner = alex, blameless postmortem due in 72h, customer comms ready to send if Bianca approves.

bianca-product: sending communication now with notes and apology + mitigation summary.

sre-alex: closing timeline: incident opened 14:48 UTC, major mitigations by 15:03 UTC, cloud reconciliation complete 15:37 UTC, returned to baseline 15:50 UTC. Assigning follow-ups: SRV synthetic checks (maria), route-propagation alerting (alex), runbook edits (jamie + alex).

jamie (oncall): thank you all. I'll file a short oncall handoff note in #eng-oncall with pointer to INC-2026-183945. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident marked resolved (status: monitoring). Postmortem scheduled.
